run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T03:39:28Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy is emitting its own span-status ERROR spans on the operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'. The dominant burst (ingress error counter 490 at 03:39:00 -> 550 at 03:42:00, i.e. +60 error spans, then 555 by 03:57:28) coincides with a payment Deployment rollout restart at 03:39:45 that replaced the single payment pod (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment) while its replacement's gRPC server did not start listening until 03:40:59.877; the payment container has no readiness/startup probe and a 20m CPU limit. In the same interval checkout's own error spans on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge rose 37 -> 59 and frontend's error spans on POST /api/checkout / grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder rose 36 -> 95, which is the upstream path behind the proxy's 5xx. Payment's own server spans carry no ERROR status and its logs show charges completing after 03:41:37, so the failure was a short availability/reconnect gap rather than payment application errors. The RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus and the alert's reported 0.0111 cannot be reproduced from the available trace series (0.000145 at 03:39:28 over 5m, 0.000223 over 10m), and Jaeger returned no traces for these services in the queried windows, so the exact trigger value and HTTP/gRPC error codes remain unresolved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy has error-status spans on span_name 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'. Raw ingress ERROR counter: 488 at 03:30:00, 490 at 03:39:00, 529 at 03:41:00, 550 at 03:42:00, 555 at 03:51:00 and still 555 at 03:57:28; 'router frontend egress' ERROR counter: 457 at 03:30:00, 496 at 03:41:00, 516 at 03:42:00.

frontend-proxy error spans were already non-zero well before the payment rollout: the first returned ingress ERROR sample at 03:18:28 was 479 (ingress UNSET 6734) and it had only risen to 490 by 03:39:00.

frontend's own error spans in the incident period are on POST /api/checkout, POST, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; the POST /api/checkout ERROR counter went 36 at 03:40:30 -> 73 at 03:41:00 -> 95 at 03:42:00 (+59 total).
checkout's own error spans are exactly oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge; both counters went 37 at 03:41:00 -> 59 at 03:42:00 (+22).

The payment Deployment was rolled out at 03:39:45: a new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 (created 03:39:45, replicas 1, annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:39:45Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment) appeared while the previous ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (same image, created 03:06:46) was scaled to 0 replicas; events show Scaled up payment-7b6bfb9fb4 0->1 at 03:39:45, SuccessfulCreate of payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht, Scaled down payment-55766d76b9 1->0, SuccessfulDelete and 'Stopping container payment' for pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 at 03:39:48. No other workload got a new ReplicaSet in the window.

The payment Deployment runs 1 replica with RollingUpdate maxSurge 25%/maxUnavailable 25%, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, and its container has readinessProbe null, startupProbe null, livenessProbe null, resources limits cpu 20m / memory 160Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 80Mi.

The replacement payment pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht started its container at 03:39:48 (restartCount 0, empty lastState) but its log's first line, 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080', is at 03:40:59.877; the first 'Charge request received.' is at 03:41:37.929 and every following charge is followed by 'Transaction complete.'.

checkout logs between 03:40:52 and 03:41:38 show repeated '[PlaceOrder]' entries with no matching 'payment went through', and successes resume at 03:41:38.928 ('payment went through', then 'order placed', email sent, Kafka write) and continue steadily afterwards.

payment's own server spans carry no error status for these requests: span_name 'charge' and 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' are STATUS_CODE_UNSET and kept increasing through the rollout (912 at 03:34:00, 1140 at 03:41:00, 1435 at 03:50:00); payment error-status spans in this window are only small internal counters (dns.lookup 1->2, tcp.connect 1->2, GET 2->4, flagd ResolveFloat 3).

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts; frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94, frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc and checkout-5dccddf8bb-c4dqt were created 03:06:45-03:06:47, and only payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht was created later (03:39:45).

Container CPU usage stayed tiny through the burst: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 0.010-0.011 cores, checkout-5dccddf8bb-c4dqt 0.004-0.006, payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht 0.006-0.020; CFS throttled-period increases were visible on frontend-proxy (84, 64, 78, 40 periods per 5m across 03:39-03:54) and on the new payment pod (1445 periods in 03:39-03:44, then 489 and 141).

Other otel-demo services' error-status span counters over 03:30-03:55 are small and near-flat (ad 24->26, fraud-detection 2->4, recommendation 3->5, payment 9->13, accounting 1), far smaller than frontend/frontend-proxy/checkout in the same window.

Error-span ratios computed from traces_span_metrics_calls_total for frontend-proxy at the alert start are far below the alert's reported 0.0111: increase over 5m at 03:39:28 = 0.000145 and over 10m = 0.000223; after the burst, increase over 5m at 03:43:28 = 0.01734.

Large frontend error counters that predate the burst were flat during it: GET 411, GET /api/data 400 and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 400 stayed unchanged from 03:38:00 to 03:44:00 while POST /api/checkout rose.

Metric discovery for service_name=frontend-proxy returned only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, and a broad {__name__=~".+"} listing returned 63 names with no http_* or rpc_* request metrics in this Prometheus.

The 03:41-03:42 error burst originates in the payment pod replacement: the only payment pod was stopped at 03:39:48 and its replacement's gRPC server was not listening until 03:40:59.877 (no readiness/startup probe makes the pod Ready at container start, and cpu limit 20m delays startup, with 1445 throttled periods in 03:39-03:44). checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls failed/blocked until reconnecting (first successful charge 03:41:37.929), so checkout returned PlaceOrder errors, frontend returned errors on POST /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy recorded ingress+egress ERROR spans on the same requests.

frontend recorded 59 failed /api/checkout requests while checkout recorded only 22 failed Charge calls (difference ~37). The extra frontend failures may be frontend->checkout calls that failed or timed out while checkout was blocked retrying payment, rather than payment returning application errors; the exact error code/text cannot be confirmed from the available data.

The alert's reported value 0.0111 is not reproducible from traces_span_metrics_calls_total (0.000145 over 5m and 0.000223 over 10m at 03:39:28), so RequestErrorRate may be computed from a different expression or data source (for example Envoy/HTTP request metrics that are not present in this Prometheus) or its startsAt may not be the condition start; this remains unverified.

payment itself shows no application failure: its 'charge' and 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' spans are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET and its logs show 'Transaction complete.' for every charge received from 03:41:37.929 onward, so the failure was availability/connection, not payment logic.

frontend-proxy, frontend and checkout pods were not restarted (restartCount 0, Running/Ready, created 03:06) and their CPU usage stayed at 0.004-0.011 cores, so a crash or resource saturation of these tiers is not supported by the evidence.

frontend-proxy's error rate was already above zero before the payment rollout (479 ingress ERROR spans at the first returned sample 03:18:28, 490 by 03:39:00), so the payment restart alone does not explain why the error rate was non-zero at alert start.
Rejected: frontend-proxy resource saturation caused the 5xx burst - CPU stayed ~0.010-0.011 cores and its CFS throttled-period increases (84, 64, 78, 40 per 5m) show no step change at 03:41-03:42.

Rejected: a frontend-proxy rollout or pod restart produced the error burst - no new frontend-proxy ReplicaSet appeared (all services' ReplicaSets except payment-7b6bfb9fb4 date from 03:06-03:08) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 has 0 restarts.

Rejected: errors of ad, fraud-detection, recommendation, accounting or payment explain the 03:41-03:42 burst - their error-status span counters are single-digit and change only by 0-2 over the whole 03:30-03:55 span, not in step with the 60 error spans seen at frontend-proxy.

Add a readiness/startup probe to the payment container (gRPC health or TCP :8080) and set RollingUpdate maxUnavailable to 0 (or raise the 20m CPU limit) so a rollout cannot send traffic to a payment pod whose gRPC server is not yet listening; this is the mechanism the timeline points to.

Inspect the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its evaluation series to confirm what produced 0.0111 at 03:39:28, and capture spans with error tags (or extend Jaeger retention) to confirm the HTTP 5xx / gRPC status codes behind the frontend-proxy ERROR spans.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no rules, so its expression, threshold window and the reported current value 0.0111 could not be verified or reproduced (computed trace-metric ratios at 03:39:28 are 0.000145 over 5m and 0.000223 over 10m).

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy (03:31-04:01 and 03:35-03:50) or checkout (03:55-04:01), so HTTP response codes, gRPC status codes/error messages, span tags and parent-child call edges are unknown.
checkout container logs contain no lines matching err|error|fail|exception|panic|warn|refus|unavail in 03:30-04:01 (0 of 3961 lines), so the exact client-side Charge failure text is unknown.
Logs of the terminated payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 are unavailable (pod deleted; previous container instance not found), so its shutdown behaviour and any pre-termination errors are unknown.

Metric samples for frontend-proxy only begin at 03:18:28 with the ingress ERROR counter already at 479 although the pod started 03:06:47; the origin and timing of those earlier errors inside 03:06-03:18 are not observable.
The change_history integration is not available, so who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart of payment at 03:39:45 (restartedAt annotation) is unknown.
kube_pod_container_resource_limits returned no data for the payment pods, so the 20m CPU limit is known only from the Deployment spec and actual throttling cannot be quantified against it.
A flagd ReplicaSet replacement occurred at 03:08:34 (flagd-869c45cb9d active, flagd-c47676d99 at 0 replicas) and could not be tied to the alert or explained from the available evidence.

No telemetry after roughly 03:57 was returned, so whether RequestErrorRate is still firing at the end of the authorized window is unknown; the last observed error increment brought the ingress ERROR counter to 555 at 03:51:00.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition (expression, lookback window, threshold) and its evaluation history to determine what produced 0.0111 at 03:39:28.
Use change history/audit logs to identify the actor and reason for the payment Deployment rollout restart at 03:39:45 (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt).

Before the next payment rollout, add a gRPC/TCP readiness probe to the payment container, set maxUnavailable to 0, and consider raising the 20m CPU limit above 20m so the server is listening before endpoints route traffic.

Collect Jaeger spans carrying error tags for POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge during 03:39-03:43 to confirm the exact status codes and error messages.
